sections.h2: Where is Upper Macungie Township, and how big has it grown?
sections.html:
Upper Macungie is a Lehigh County township about 11.5 miles southwest of Allentown, 60.8 miles northwest of Philadelphia and 99.2 miles west of New York City. It spans 26.3 square miles and was created in 1832 when Macungie Township was divided into Upper and Lower Macungie. Wikipedia lists seven villages: Breinigsville, Fogelsville, Krocksville, Kuhnsville, Newtown, Ruppsville and Trexlertown.

The growth numbers are the story here. The township counted 13,895 people in 2000, 20,063 in 2010 and 26,377 in 2020, a gain of 44.4 percent in the first decade and 31.5 percent in the second. The 2020 census found 9,313 households with an average size of 2.65 people. A township that added so many residents in two decades has plenty of newer housing, so look at what comparable recent homes on your side of the township listed for.

The ZIP codes are 18031, 18051, 18087, 18104 and 18106. Lower Macungie lies to the southeast and South Whitehall to the northeast, while Maxatawny and Longswamp Townships in Berks County border the township on the west and southwest.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and schools in Upper Macungie affect a listing?
sections.html:
Interstate 78 and U.S. 22 cross at exit 49 in Fogelsville, where Pennsylvania Route 100 also meets them. U.S. 222 cuts from southwest to northeast, and PA 100, Interstate 476 and PA 863 carry traffic north and south. Schantz Road links several industrial and commerce parks across the township. As of 2022 the township had 182.81 miles of public roads, with 135.94 miles maintained by the township, 45.97 by PennDOT and 0.90 by the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission. LANta bus routes 213, 218 and 322 serve it.

The Parkland School District covers the township. Grades 9 through 12 attend Parkland High School, and most middle schoolers go to Springhouse Middle School, except those in the far north. Fogelsville, Fred J. Jaindl and Veterans Memorial Elementary Schools are located in the township. Parkland Community Library on Walbert Avenue is free to residents of Upper Macungie, North Whitehall and South Whitehall townships.

  • Say how far the house is from I-78, Route 100 and the warehouse corridor along Schantz Road.
  • Name the elementary school only after confirming the attendance zone with Parkland.
  • Mention the library, parks and the Lehigh Valley hospital campus if they are close.

sections.h2: Does the weather or land in Upper Macungie matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Winters are cold and summers are warm. The township sits in a hot-summer humid continental climate, in USDA hardiness zone 6b, and the average monthly temperature in Fogelsville runs from 28.5 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 73.3 degrees in July. That means a heating system, roof and insulation are real selling points, and an aging boiler or furnace will show up in an inspection.

Water flows to Little Lehigh Creek and Jordan Creek, which both feed the Lehigh River, so walk the lot for low spots and check where downspouts discharge. The township's permit list includes a Low Pressure Sewer System Connection form. If your house is on one, expect buyers to ask how it works and who maintains it, and get the details from the township before you list.

Lehigh County runs a Clean and Green program that assesses qualifying farm and forest land on use value. If your parcel is enrolled, the county posts a conveyance form for sales, so ask the Assessment Office before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect selling in Upper Macungie?
sections.html:
No resale inspection is listed among the Permit Department's forms. The department, at 7540 Windsor Drive, Suite 311, is open weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and it enforces the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code. Its form list covers basements, decks, kitchens, bathrooms, roof re-shingling, water heaters, HVAC replacement, pools, oil tank removal and sheds, and it also lists a Business Use and Occupancy application. A house sale is not on that list, so ask the Permit Department whether your address needs anything for transfer.

The state building code changed on January 1, 2026, when the 2021 ICC code series became enforceable. Work under contracts signed before that date could use the older 2018 code if the permit was filed by June 30, 2026, and anything signed or filed after that must meet the 2021 code. If you have an unfinished project, ask the township which code applies to it.

  • Zoning permits are issued when a use or structure conforms to the zoning ordinance.
  • A denied zoning permit can be appealed to the Zoning Hearing Board, which usually meets on the second and fourth Wednesdays at 6:30 p.m.
  • Appeals must reach the township about four weeks before the hearing.
  • The township is rewriting its zoning ordinance, and printed copies of the current one cost $35.

sections.h2: What does Lehigh County charge and record when an Upper Macungie house sells?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds, Room 122 of the Courthouse at 455 W. Hamilton Street in Allentown, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays (610-782-3162). Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent realty transfer tax, and a local share is collected at recording. Ask the Recorder for the local rate that applies to an Upper Macungie address, because the local tax can be shared between the township and the school district.

Upper Macungie recording and appeal facts. Sources: Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds and Assessment Office, Upper Macungie Township

Transfers between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and siblings are generally exempt, and statements of value must accompany any transfer that claims an exemption or does not state full consideration. The county notes that a transfer and price cannot be kept out of the newspaper, since deeds are public.

sections.h2: How does the Lehigh County assessment and appeal work for Upper Macungie owners?
sections.html:
The Lehigh County Assessment Office sets values using a base year of 2013, the year of the last countywide reassessment, with a ratio of 100 percent of fair market value. Appeals go to the Board of Assessment Appeals. The Board accepts only an original signed appeal received on or before August 1 with the filing fee, or an interim appeal by the date printed on a change notice. It will not treat a postmark or a fax as proof of timely filing, so hand-deliver the form or send it early.

Act 29 of 2026, signed on July 20, 2026, requires owners who are not owner-occupants to file contact information with the county within 30 days of buying a property. If your buyer is an investor, they will have that task after closing. The Assessment Office is at Room 517 of the Government Center, 17 South Seventh Street in Allentown, reachable at 610-782-3038.

Township and school tax rates come from the township office and the Parkland School District tax office, so pull your latest bill before you price the house.

sections.h2: What are my choices if I want to sell an Upper Macungie house fast?
sections.html:
You have three routes: list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer from a company that buys as-is. Upper Macungie has many newer houses, so condition matters, and a cash buyer may be the better fit when a property needs work.

  • List if the house is updated and you can wait through showings and a buyer's financing.
  • Sell for cash if you inherited the property, own a tenant-occupied house or need to close on your own schedule.
  • Gather permit records for any basement, deck or kitchen project, since buyers and title companies look for them.

Ask for written offers, compare net proceeds after transfer tax and fees, and confirm who pays the transfer tax before you sign.

faqs.q: Does Upper Macungie require an inspection before I sell my house?
faqs.a: The Permit Department's forms list does not include a residential resale inspection. Ask the Permit Department at 7540 Windsor Drive whether anything applies to your address, and close any open permits before listing.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Upper Macungie Township?
faqs.a: Parkland School District. Students in grades 9 through 12 attend Parkland High School, and most middle schoolers attend Springhouse Middle School. Confirm your attendance zone with the district.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a Lehigh County assessment?
faqs.a: August 1 each year for annual appeals. The Board accepts only an original signed appeal with the filing fee received on or before that date, and it does not accept faxes or postmarks as proof.

faqs.q: What is the realty transfer tax on an Upper Macungie sale?
faqs.a: The state charges 1 percent, and a local share is added at recording. Ask the Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds at 610-782-3162 for the local rate that applies to your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in the Clean and Green program in Upper Macungie?
faqs.a: Ask the Lehigh County Assessment Office before you sign. Clean and Green is a preferential assessment program that generally needs ten acres in agricultural use, agricultural reserve or forest reserve, and the county posts a conveyance form for enrolled land.
